claim:
Round 6 rewrote T-V6-64 (V06 l. 4187): "the arch vaults follow their spans at every batch (a chamber under every standing `vault` span no wall stands over, none under a fallen one or under a wall, §2.7's crossing table)". "None under a fallen one" is kept from the old text. Every home of the rule keeps the chamber under a fallen span, `collapsed`:
- V04 §3.5.4 (d) (1)–(3) (V04 l. 1695–1716): each `vault` span no wall stands over "has one chamber", and "its closure follows its span …: `collapsed` where the span's `state` is `ruined` or `cleared` … or where a bounding support's `state` is `ruined` or `cleared`". (3) removes one only where the span no longer exists, is `open`, or has a wall over it.
- V06's own §3.2 (l. 1037–1040): the reconcile brings each raised way to "a chamber for each standing `vault` span no wall stands over, a collapse under a `ruined` or `cleared` span".
- §4.11's `DeclineOp` raised member (base l. 8764): "breach and dismantle collapse the span's arch-vault chambers in the same batch (V04), and removal deletes them".
- T-V4-62 (V04 l. 3155): "each `collapsed` exactly when V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2) says so (the span's or a bounding support's `state` `ruined` or `cleared`…)". T-V4-63's frame clause, written this round: "a vault laid in a `ruined` or `cleared` one `collapsed`".
So on H-AQUA, whose lapse breaches spans (T-V6-61: "the vaults collapse with their span in the same batch"), T-V6-64 fails a correct build at the batch that breaches a `vault` span. A builder who keeps T-V6-64 deletes the chamber when its span falls, against V04 and §4.11. Two units state two outcomes for one case, so this is MAJOR. VAT6-r6-01 raises the same reading of "standing" in T-V4-63. The two bars should take one wording.
required_change: T-V6-64: "(a chamber under every standing `vault` span no wall stands over, none under a fallen one or under a wall, §2.7's crossing table)" → "(a chamber under every `vault` span no wall stands over — open under a standing one, `collapsed` under one whose span or a bounding support is `ruined` or `cleared` (V04 §3.5.4 (d) (2)) — and none under a wall (§2.7's crossing table) or where the span no longer exists)".

claim: An epoch's founding across a drawn or locked wall (C-wall-raised x C-raised-lock at an epoch). V06 §3.19 (5) (V06 l. 2815-2822) solves a founded course with 'Locked, pinned and declared entities, dossier-listed buildings, every other raised way's supports, enceinte towers and gates ... impassable, filtered before any draw'. In the same sentence: 'a course meeting a standing curtain meets it by §2.7's crossing table — an aqueduct *over the band*'. The crossing table's row W2 (a hand `drawWall`) sends a raised way created later to W1·C1, *over the band* 'or V06's founding', with 'nothing of the wall ... written' (base l. 2603, 2686-2690). Every drawn wall is 'locked by default' and every declared entity is held (§7.2, l. 10810-10820). So on a document whose user drew or locked a ring, the readings split. V06's list makes the ring impassable to an epoch aqueduct, which then never finds a course; its terminal lies 'inside the outermost enceinte' (V06 §3.19 (6)), so it waits (`raised.waited`) at every epoch. The table crosses the ring on a span, writing nothing of it. The same list makes a drawn ground way impassable to a founded deck passing over it, while §7.4's raised-way row lets a deck pass over a locked way ('a raised way over a locked way keeps its span `open`', l. 11447). This is a common path: a user who draws the walls and runs epochs at CITY gets no aqueduct from one builder and one from another. VDC6-01 (determinism) is the hand-edit sibling at §7.1's lock row; this is the epoch path, at a different home.

claim: T-V6-47 (V6-21, l. 4170) takes T110-2 (7) with its own script: 'a `vault` span in the circuit's band breached and a support by the band dismantled by scripted `DeclineOp`s (as its lapse's salvage would, V06 §3.19.2 (3); E3's ops)'. A trace crosses an aqueduct only under a span (*beneath*), so the supports by the band bound the breached span, and only that span is breached. V06 §3.19.2 (3) dismantles only 'a support both of whose spans are ruined or cleared', and T-V6-61 holds '0 supports cleared while a span beside them stands' on H-AQUA. The script, as written, leaves a standing span on a cleared support; the base's (7) avoids this by making a span over the band `ruined` as well. The test also omits the later-laid order. Row W1·C5 (and W1·C3) names T-V6-47 for 'laid after the fall, through a `cleared` ring as open ground', which V06 §3.7.6 (5)'s new `cleared` clause governs. T-V6-47 runs only the order in which the circuit comes first; the base's (7) holds the other order ('in the cells' own order').
